Proposal and estimate for Sridhar Patnaik, GreyBoard Consulting (Nexus360)

Researching the real owner of Chhattisgarh builders, then WhatsApp outreach where a business-published number exists

We research who is behind each builder on the public RERA register, where public evidence supports it. Where a business has published a WhatsApp-capable number, we send two fixed, approved messages with a personalised page and video. No AI conversation with an owner: every genuine reply goes to you.

What you get

  • A researched builder list: the owner or decision-maker where public evidence supports it, with a confidence label, source and date. A person checks every record.
  • Two fixed WhatsApp messages, a personalised page and a 17-second video, for builders with a WhatsApp-capable published number.
  • A dashboard, and every genuine reply handed to you.
  • Every claim marked Fact, Estimate, Assumption or Opinion.

What it costs Proposed

₹35,000

  • Or research only: ₹12,000 for 50 builders.
  • WhatsApp fees at cost: about ₹30 to ₹200 for the pilot, capped at ₹500.

  • Two short screen recordings, your logo, a voice choice and written permission to use the Nexus360 name.
  • A WhatsApp number for hand-off alerts, your job title as you want it shown, and your customer list.
  • Optional: CRM test access.

How it works

Five steps from the public register to your phone. A person checks the research before anything is sent, and you take every genuine reply. Only two messages go out.

  1. 1
    RERA register shortlist by rules

    We read the public Chhattisgarh RERA list (one request, no login) and apply rules you can see: three districts, valid registration, housing, private builders, not your customers. Today that leaves 72 builders.

    AUTOMATED
  2. 2
    Real-owner research and enrichment

    For each builder we look for who is behind it, where public evidence supports it: its own site, company records and the filing. Each record carries VERIFIED, LIKELY or UNKNOWN, a source link and a date. A person checks it before any message.

    A PERSON CHECKS
  3. 3
    WhatsApp message, page and video

    Only where the business published a WhatsApp-capable number: a short message from IV Infotech's line with a personalised page and a 17-second video. You approve the wording first. Every message has a STOP line. Others are not messaged.

    AUTOMATED
  4. 4
    Follow-up and tracking

    One fixed follow-up if there is no reply and no STOP. The dashboard shows sent, delivered, read, page opened and replied. When a builder replies or taps a button, all automatic messages to that builder stop.

    AUTOMATED
  5. 5
    Genuine reply handed to you

    A typed reply or button tap from a person (not STOP, a greeting or an auto-reply) is alerted to you on WhatsApp with the exact words, the builder, the owner and what they opened. No AI conversation with an owner: you answer.

    YOU

You said the RERA number is often not the real owner. Our test partly agrees.

On six register pages, the filed contact was the promoter or managing director himself in 3 (in 2 of those the filed email looked like an adviser's), a salaried officer in 2, and unknown in 1. So it is often an officer or another person's mailbox, and sometimes the owner's own mobile. We start at the register, not stop there. Fact, 6 builders Our reading

The first message Sample wording

Hi Rakesh, IV Infotech here, writing for Sridhar Patnaik of Nexus360 (ERP and CRM for builders). We saw Sample Residency in Raipur on the RERA register and made you a short video.
One question: do you track site indents and stock in Excel or in software today?Reply STOP to opt out. Buttons: Excel, Software, Stop.

The follow-up Sample wording

Hi Rakesh, IV Infotech again, for Sridhar Patnaik (Nexus360). If site requests for Sample Residency still go to the office by phone or WhatsApp, Sridhar can show you the indent-to-purchase-order flow in a 20-minute demo. Reply YES and he will call you.Sent only if there is no reply and no STOP. Reply STOP to opt out.

You agree the final wording on Day 6. The Hindi needs a native-speaker check.

When a builder replies

  • A typed reply or a button tap from a person is alerted to you on WhatsApp with the exact words, the builder and the owner. You answer; all automatic messages to that builder stop.
  • STOP and automatic greetings are logged, not handed over. STOP is honoured.
  • Replies on your own number. The page's "Book a demo on WhatsApp" button opens a chat on your own number, which we cannot see. We log the tap and stop the follow-up. You log or forward those conversations and we count them by hand.
  • Not built yet: the reply rule for this account, so every reply on our line goes only to you. We set it up and test it before any send.

The demo (3 of 3): the page and the video

You asked whether the personalised page and video can be made for Nexus360. They can. These samples use your public website and fictional builder names. Amber marks are filled per builder or by you.

What changes per builder

Only the title block (builder, project, city, RERA number, date) and the first line of the WhatsApp message. The video, the product lines, your name and your number stay the same.

Where each line comes from

Every product statement is taken from nexus360.in. You confirm or strike each one. The grey boxes stay empty until you send recordings.

Built for an operator reading first

RERA numbers often reach an operator, so the page has a button: "Reading this for someone else? Forward it to the owner". Nothing is sent until the builder presses Send.

No savings, ROI or time-saved claims, no other builder's results, no price.

Voice. Your own voice for four short Hindi lines (our recommendation), English, or captions only. No AI voice unless you ask.

The two-week pilot

A fixed-price test on 50 builders over 14 days, plus a 3-day reply window, with the report on Day 17. It mainly tests coverage, delivery and hand-off, not the reply rate: a reply-rate read needs about 150 builders. It promises no customers.

What we do

  • 50 builders chosen with you, each with a research record checked by a person.
  • WhatsApp from IV Infotech's line to builders with a WhatsApp-capable published number: up to 2 messages each, plus a retry if delivery fails. The others are not messaged.
  • Every genuine reply to you. No AI conversation with an owner. A dashboard and a Day 17 report.
  • Pass and fail rules agreed in writing before Day 0. What we need from you: page 9.

The channel: WhatsApp, from IV Infotech's line

The WhatsApp Business account is ours. Meta expects opt-in, and a number on a builder's site or the RERA register is not an opt-in. Some messages will not arrive, and Meta can limit the line if recipients block or report it. Our own first campaign: 2 of 7 cold templates on time, 1 about four hours late, 3 failed (Meta refused 2 under a per-recipient marketing limit, 1 undeliverable). So we send only to numbers the business published, 10 to 25 a day Assumption, with a STOP line in every message, and stop and tell you if Meta shows a warning.

How we measure, and the pass and fail rules agreed in advance

MeasureHow it is countedPassIf not met
1 Owner coverageBuilders with a named owner or decision-maker and a source (Verified or Likely). Our test: 4 of 6.20 of 50 or more (40%)Narrow the segment or add research before any monthly run.
2 Builders with a WhatsApp-capable published numberA published number wired for WhatsApp, or a promoter's RERA-filed mobile. Our test: 1 of 6 wired, 1 more RERA mobile.15 of 50 or more (30%)WhatsApp alone does not fit this market. The first touch moves to a person phoning the office line.
3 DeliveryMessages delivered to owner-level numbers, divided by messages sent to them. Not "on time". Our first campaign: 2 of 7 on time.60% or moreChange the number, the channel or the first touch.
4 Genuine owner-level repliesA real two-way reply from an owner or decision-maker, typed or a button tap, including those you log or forward from your own number. STOP, auto-replies, greetings and wrong numbers do not count.1 or moreNone: we do not recommend the monthly run. We offer the research-only list, or we stop.
5 Line health and hand-offMeta quality rating and any restriction, read on Day 17. Each genuine reply alerted to you, with the minutes from reply to alert.No warning or restriction. Every genuine reply alertedPause sends and use a separate number. We report each miss and fix the route.

Decision rule. If measures 1 to 5 are met, including at least one genuine reply, we recommend a second batch of about 150 builders, the first month of the run, as the real reply-rate test. With no genuine reply from owner-level messages we recommend the research-only list or stopping, not the monthly run. A miss on another measure means we change that first. We also report the cost per genuine reply (pilot fee plus WhatsApp fees, divided by genuine replies), with no pass mark. We decide together on the Day 17 call. The fee is fixed. Second messages go out on Days 10 to 13, so a later reply may miss the count.

The test is small. With 50 builders, perhaps 5 to 20 messages reach an owner-level number Assumption. If none of 13 messages gets a reply, the true reply rate could still be up to about 21% Estimate. A reliable reply rate needs 100 to 150 builders, which is one month of the run.

Sources. Meta WhatsApp Business Messaging Policy (whatsappbusiness.com/policy) and pricing (developers.facebook.com/docs/whatsapp/pricing). Our first campaign: 7 cold templates, 2 on time, 1 about 4 hours late, 3 failed, 1 silent for 3 days (our records, 20 Oct 2026). One-sided 95% bound for the 21%. The 5 to 20 range and 10 to 25 a day are our assumptions. The 1-of-6 figure is from our 6-builder test (page 3).

Alternative to B: shared risk Option

Instead of B you can pay ₹20,000 a month plus ₹4,000 for each demo held with an owner-level contact (15 minutes or more, confirmed by you). You choose after the pilot. Same 150 builders and the same service.

Up to 4 demos a month this costs less than one employee (₹36,900); at 2 demos it costs the same as B. B itself costs about 0.8 times one employee, but it does a different job: it does not close deals or build relationships.

WhatsApp fees, passed through at cost

Meta charges per delivered marketing message: ₹0.8631 in India, ₹1.02 with 18% GST. Our provider may bill more, so we allow up to ₹1.29. We pass on exactly what we are billed, with no markup, and ask you before passing the cap. Hand-off alerts are inside it.

Pilot: 100 to 150 messages if every builder had a WhatsApp-capable number (50 builders, 1 to 1.5 numbers each, 2 messages each); likely fewer, as only a minority does. 30% to 100% delivered = about ₹30 to ₹200. Month: 300 to 450 messages, about ₹90 to ₹580. Estimate

Day 0 is the day we have your written approval. We count in days from Day 0 because Meta's approval of a number or template is outside our control. If one is late, we tell you the same day and agree a revised plan. Nothing is sent to any builder before you approve the messages on Day 6. Second messages go out on Days 10 to 13, so replies are counted until Day 17. The timings are our assumptions Assumption.

Who does what

Our team

Checks every research record before the first send, sets up and tests the reply route, and reports the minutes from each reply to its alert. Any phone call or conversation with an owner is human.

The AI

Researches, drafts, sends the two fixed messages you approved and logs everything. It does not answer a reply, phone, negotiate or close. A reply or a button tap ends all automatic messages to that builder.

You

Approve the list and, on Day 6, the exact messages. Take every genuine reply. Join a 15-minute weekly review Assumption. Agree the pass and fail rules in writing before Day 0.

What we need from you

  • Positioning (Day 0). Who you sell to, the one thing a builder should remember, a yes or no on each product line, including "20+ projects" and "200+ people", and your job title as you want it shown. It is not on nexus360.in, so we show none until you confirm.
  • Footage (by Day 3). Two to three screenshots, or two short recordings with sample data: an indent approval with its checks (6 to 8 s), and a lead, follow-up and payment schedule (5 to 6 s). Your logo.
  • Permission (by Day 3). The Nexus360 name in messages and in the WhatsApp display name. Any customer name, with that customer's written yes.
  • Hand-off (by Day 3). A WhatsApp number for alerts, your reply hours or a calendar link, demo length, and whether it is free.
  • Your customer list, so we do not contact existing customers, and a voice choice: your own voice for four short Hindi lines, English, or captions only.
  • Replies on your own number. Log or forward the page-button taps that became conversations. We count them by hand.
  • Optional. Your numbers for the comparison. CRM test access: a test account and API notes. We cannot price that until we see the API; it is in no price here.

Limits, compliance, terms and next steps

Limits

  • The real owner's direct number is often not public. In our test it was found for none of six, and a number wired for WhatsApp for one of six. A builder with no WhatsApp-capable published number is researched but not messaged in the pilot.
  • We do not promise replies, demos or customers. Our first campaign contacted 9 builders and has no confirmed genuine reply yet. That is too few to conclude anything.
  • Delivery depends on Meta. 2 of 7 of our own cold templates arrived on time.
  • Madhya Pradesh is not automated. Its RERA site's robots.txt disallows bots. We could ask MP RERA for permission or build a list by hand, later. Neither is in this proposal.
  • "Small or medium" is a stand-in until we use filed project cost and a group check. Director lookups are done by hand in the pilot; automating them needs a licence that is not priced here.
  • Correction to our first message. It quoted "92+ staff hours" and "₹23,000+ monthly overhead saved". We cannot source those figures, so please disregard them. The pilot is a 14-day test, not a finished deployment.

Compliance Risk summary, not legal advice

  • Public data only. Contact details only where the business published them (its own site, an ad or the RERA register), stored with source and date. No bought lists. Numbers are masked in reports.
  • Opt-out. Every message carries a STOP line. STOP is honoured and added to a suppression list.
  • Meta policy. WhatsApp expects opt-in. Messages to published numbers carry a risk of limits or a block. The account is ours, so we carry that risk.
  • DPDP Act 2023. Data made public by the person, or by someone legally bound to publish it, may fall outside the Act (section 3). Director names from third-party listings may not. Most duties start about May 2027. We follow the practice now: a notice on the page, takedown on request, a deletion date for unverified contact data. Ask your own counsel.
  • Sender. We recommend a separate +91 WhatsApp number with a clear display name, subject to Meta's approval and your permission, so a restriction does not reach our other lines.

Terms Proposed

  • Payment: To be agreed. We suggest 50% on written approval and 50% at the Day 17 report.
  • Credit: Because this is a first deployment, the pilot is priced close to our cost. In return we ask for your written permission to describe the results, without naming any builder, as a reference. A research-only list bought first is credited in full against the pilot if you continue within 30 days.
  • Skipping the pilot: month 1 of the run adds a one-time set-up of about ₹35,000.
  • Data and exit: Your lists and records are exported to you at the end of the pilot and on request, as CSV: the research records, the send and reply log and the dashboard data. Either side can stop at any month end. Retention and deletion of builder contact data are agreed in writing before Day 0.
  • The pool is finite. About 424 small promoters are on the register in the three districts, 798 in the state, counting registrations of any age. At 150 unworked builders a month that lasts roughly 3 to 5 months. After that about 4 builders a month newly qualify, so we would propose a lower fee.

Next steps

  1. Walkthrough. A 15-minute screen share of the dashboard, the builder page and the video storyboard.
  2. You choose the pilot (recommended), the research-only list first, or a different structure.
  3. You send the inputs on page 9 and confirm the pass and fail rules in writing. We confirm price, scope and Day 0 in writing.
  4. Day 0. We start. Nothing reaches a builder until you approve the messages.
